bounded_lifecycle_probe.serialization_path: Actual worker.main request validation, measure, SharedFailure handling and JSON serialization; actual Docker.stage parser with subprocess result replaced; controller exercised for the successful simulated lifecycle.

limits: Correctness-only source gate for this exact frozen inventory; privilege and isolation sign-off belongs to the independent security review.
No real Redis, Docker process, image preparation/build, real case, Go build/test, commit or publication was performed.
The main agent's full 171-harness/21-script suite, 81 canonical Go-race checks and vet/pin verification were not duplicated or independently claimed as passing.

The bounded lifecycle probes use an in-memory model-backed command facade, fake environment receipts and fake process output; they are not independent target Redis/Lua execution or actual ACL-parsing evidence.
Native Python 3.12.7 timings are not target-image resource or 30-second real-stage performance acceptance.
Builder checks are static COPY/allowlist/import-closure checks, not Dockerignore-parser or built-image validation. Test-class-only imports are excluded from the Spider vector-entry-point closure.
Two logical owners and two runs are interleaved by one fixed ledger executor; no simultaneous physical-worker, network-I/O or publication behavior is asserted.
Positive cancellation and reversed-order traces remain offline controls. Runtime cancellation is exercised only as expected errors in the fixed finish trace.
Mutable handoff documentation still describing the prior offline checkpoint was acknowledged as pending the main agent's post-review update, not treated as an executable-source defect.
next_gate: Correctness GO for image/CI preparation, with main verification and independent security review remaining separate gates. This review grants no build, case execution, commit or publication authority.

positive_observations.summary: Resume reconstruction binds probe history, changed Redis run identity, immutable BOOT, observed setup time, complete combined setup digest and all 60 setup counters before measurement.

Each fixed transition is dispatched once; replies and whole-database state are checked before appending a receipt. Successful and failed receipts are reconstructed from the observed prefix, preserving only validated rows after ambiguous dispatch.

The shared case adds only the explicit 90-position bound. Whole-DB membership, fixed schema/cardinality, typed values, absolute expiries and finite SCAN budget remain fail-closed for older bounds as well.

Counter projections contain 24 fields per actor plus 12 fields across four distinct scopes, not duplicate per-actor shared scope counters; leases, history and both physical/logical reservation expiries remain bound.

The previously reviewed oracle retains its transition semantics, ordered observed-time prefix, 30-second span and live-lease bounds; the new validated helper does not replace the fixture-validation boundary.
SharedFailure is validated and serialized by the actual worker entry point rather than flattened to an unstructured error.

The Docker parser and controller retain only validated shared failure receipts, while cleanup still stops/waits/removes the worker before a fresh revocation helper; setup failure does not enter measurement.

scope.included: Executable lifecycle plumbing, observed/model-time prefix enforcement, combined two-run setup, whole-DB reader bounds, counters, BOOT/probe bindings, strict serialized failure prefixes, ambiguity handling, malformed values and history/expiry forgeries, older-case regression exposure and setup-failure cleanup coordination.

summary: No correctness blockers or actionable correctness findings in the frozen lifecycle integration. The complete-state verification and closed receipt reconstruction are strong, and targeted malformed/ambiguous boundary probes passed without retries or false success.
